'''Flórián György Albert''' (15 September 1941 – 31 October 2011) was a Hungarian professional [[association football|football]] player, manager and sports official, who was named [[European Footballer of the Year]] in 1967. Nicknamed "The Emperor",<ref name=fifa1>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/archive/southafrica2010/awards/bestyoungplayer/player=174330/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110314051811/http://www.fifa.com/worldcup/archive/southafrica2010/awards/bestyoungplayer/player=174330/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=14 March 2011|title=World Cup Best Young Player – 1962 Florian ALBERT (HUN)|publisher=FIFA.com|access-date=3 November 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/sport/amateur-football/2011/11/01/hungarian-great-florian-albert-dies-aged-70-100252-29696040/|title=Hungarian great Florian Albert dies aged 70|publisher=Liverpool Echo|date=1 November 2011|access-date=3 November 2011}}</ref> he played as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]], and has been described as one of the most elegant footballers of all time.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.uefa.com/uefa/aboutuefa/organisation/history/obituaries/newsid=1707397.html|title=Hungarian Ballon d'Or winner Albert dies|publisher=[[UEFA]]|date=31 October 2011|access-date=31 October 2011|archive-date=1 November 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111101113336/http://www.uefa.com/uefa/aboutuefa/organisation/history/obituaries/newsid=1707397.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

A club legend of [[Ferencvárosi TC]], Albert joined the team as a schoolboy and [[List of one-club men in association football|spent his whole playing career]] at ''Fradi''. He also starred for Hungary, winning 75 international caps and scoring 31 goals. He was joint top-scorer at the 1962 World Cup with four goals and played a key role in Hungary's third-place finish at the European Championship in 1964.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/755/europe/2011/10/31/2736252/hungary-ferencvaros-legend-florian-albert-dies-aged-70|title=Hungary & Ferencvaros legend Florian Albert dies aged 70|publisher=goal.com|date=31 October 2011|access-date=3 November 2011|archive-date=1 November 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111101162525/http://www.goal.com/en/news/755/europe/2011/10/31/2736252/hungary-ferencvaros-legend-florian-albert-dies-aged-70|url-status=live}}</ref>

He stayed loyal to Ferencváros after his retirement as well, actively participated in the club's life and also held administrative positions. From 2007 the stadium of Ferencváros bore his name, until 2014 when the new stadium of the team was constructed, named “[[Ferencváros Stadion|Groupama Arena]]”. A statue was erected in his honour in front of the stadium in 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nemzetisport.hu/labdarugo-nb-i/2014/08/fradi-lelepleztek-az-albert-szobrot-megnyilt-a-muzeum-kep|title=Fradi: leleplezték a stadion előtt az Albert-szobrot, megnyílt a múzeum|publisher=Nemzeti Sport|date=2014-08-31|language=hu|access-date=2026-02-10}}</ref>

Albert died in October 2011, aged 70, in a hospital in Budapest after complications following heart surgery carried out a few days earlier.<ref name=obituary /><ref name=yahoo>{{cite web|url=http://uk.eurosport.yahoo.com/31102011/58/world-football-hungarian-great-albert-dies.html|title=World Football - Hungarian great Albert dies|publisher=Yahoo! Eurosport|date=31 October 2011|access-date=3 November 2011}}</ref>

==Early life==
The son of a blacksmith, Albert was born and brought up in the little town of [[Hercegszántó]] near the border with the former [[Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia|Yugoslavia]], where he got his first taste of the game playing with his two brothers. His mother was of [[Šokci]] origin. She died when he was two.<ref name="Hrvatski glasnik">{{in lang|hr}} [https://web.archive.org/web/20140729021354/http://www.croatica.hu/fileadmin/glasnik/2007/glasnik33.pdf Hrvatski glasnik br.33/2007.] Počasni građanin Santova, 16 August 2007, p. 5</ref> When the family later moved to [[Budapest]], Albert participated on a talent day held by [[Ferencvárosi TC|Ferencváros]].<ref name=hetek>{{cite web|url=http://www.hetek.hu/interju/200008/albert_florian_a_jo_foci_titkarol|title=Albert Flórián a jó foci titkáról|trans-title=Flórán Albert about the secret of good football|publisher=Hetek|date=5 August 2000|access-date=7 November 2011|language=hu|archive-date=14 July 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714205307/http://www.hetek.hu/interju/200008/albert_florian_a_jo_foci_titkarol|url-status=live}}</ref> He impressed the coaches and was selected by the club. Albert was 11 years old at the time.<ref name="Hrvatski glasnik" />

==Career==
Albert spent his entire club career with [[Ferencvárosi TC]], where he played from 1952<ref name="Hrvatski glasnik" /> to 1974. He came through the ranks quickly and made his debut in the senior team on 2 November 1958 against [[Diósgyőri VTK|Diósgyőr]], in a match in which he hit the back of the net two times. The forward was also spotted by [[Hungary national football team|Hungarian national team]] manager [[Lajos Baróti]] in a youth match between Hungary and Yugoslavia,<ref name=film>{{cite web|url=http://videotar.mtv.hu/Videok/2011/10/31/20/Az_utolso_Ulloi_uti_Csaszar__portrefilm_Albert.aspx|title=Az utolsó Üllői úti Császár – portrait film about Flórián Albert|publisher=Hungarian Television Video Archives|access-date=7 November 2011|language=hu|archive-date=1 November 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111101143136/http://videotar.mtv.hu/Videok/2011/10/31/20/Az_utolso_Ulloi_uti_Csaszar__portrefilm_Albert.aspx|url-status=live}}</ref> and not much later Albert already received his first call-up. His first appearance in the national selection came on 28 June 1959 against Sweden, who finished runners-up in the World Cup a year earlier. Albert contributed with two assist to Hungary's 3–2 win over the Scandinavians. He scored 31 goals in 75 [[cap (sport)|caps]] for the Hungarian team, with them he has collected the bronze medal on both of the Olympic Games in 1960 and the European Championship in 1964.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.olympedia.org/athletes/25658 |title=Flórián Albert |work=Olympedia |access-date=10 December 2021 |archive-date=10 December 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211210145735/https://www.olympedia.org/athletes/25658 |url-status=live }}</ref> At the [[FIFA World Cup 1962|1962 World Cup]], despite Hungary being knocked out in the quarter-finals, Albert, tied with five others, managed to win the [[FIFA World Cup awards#Golden Boot|Golden Boot Award]] with four goals.

On club level, his biggest success came in 1965, when in the [[Inter-Cities Fairs Cup]], Ferencváros, that knocked-out among others [[AS Roma]] and [[Manchester United F.C.]] en route to the final, triumphed over [[Juventus FC]] 1–0 in the decisive match and obtained the cup title.<ref name=obituary />

{{Rquote|left|Florian was an extremely elegant footballer with extraordinary skill and ball control. These qualities ensured that he was highly respected by his opponents. I remember his sensational performance in the game against Brazil at the FIFA World Cup in 1966 in England, which cemented his standing as one of the world's top players.|FIFA president [[Sepp Blatter]] about Albert<ref name=fifa2>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/classicfootball/news/newsid=1535398.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111103192627/http://www.fifa.com/classicfootball/news/newsid=1535398.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=3 November 2011|title=The eternal elegance of Florian Albert|publisher=FIFA.com|date=31 October 2011|access-date=3 November 2011}}</ref>}}

Albert appeared in his next World event in 1966 in England, where he produced an excellent display against Brazil in a duel that is regarded as one of the greatest matches in the history of the World Cup.<ref name=fifa1 /><ref name=fifa2 /> The Magyars, after losing to Portugal in their first round encounter, entered a must-win match against Brazil. Hungary eventually beat the South Americans 3–1, to keep their hopes alive, and Albert, who received a standing ovation from the supporters, made the fans forget the absence of Pelé with his performance.<ref name=fifa2 /> By winning their final group match, Hungary made it to the quarter-finals, just to fall short against the Soviet Union.

The year 1967 was a special one for Albert, who not only won the Hungarian Championship with Ferencváros and collected the Hungarian Player of the Year title, but in December first celebrated the birth of his son, and later he was awarded the [[Ballon d'Or]] in recognition of his outstanding attributes.<ref name=fifa1 /><ref name=fifa2 /> Albert topped the voting with 68 points, twenty-eight ahead of [[Bobby Charlton]], who came second.<ref name=hetek />

In 1968 Albert appeared in the Inter-Cities Fairs Cup final again, this time against [[Leeds United]], but lost by a one-goal margin (0–1). On 15 June 1969, in a World Cup qualifier against Denmark, Albert collided with Knud Engedal, goalkeeper of the Scandinavians, and suffered a serious fractured leg injury. Following that he was sidelined for almost a year and could never win back his form any more.<ref name=origo>{{cite web|url=http://www.origo.hu/sport/magyarfoci/20111031-elhunyt-albert-florian-az-egyetlen-magyar-aranylabdas.html|title=Elhunyt Albert Flórián, az egyetlen magyar aranylabdás|trans-title=Flórián Albert, the only Hungarian Golden Ball winner deceased|publisher=Origo|date=31 October 2011|access-date=31 October 2011|archive-date=1 November 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111101014831/http://www.origo.hu/sport/magyarfoci/20111031-elhunyt-albert-florian-az-egyetlen-magyar-aranylabdas.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Albert returned into action in the Hungarian Championship on 27 April 1970 against Salgótarján and on 4 April 1971 he played his first international match after the injury, a friendly match against Austria. His final major event was the 1972 European Championship, where he captured fourth place with Hungary, recording two appearances in the tournament. In the same year he captured the Hungarian Cup title for the first time, thus making his collection of domestic silverware complete.

Albert played his final league match on 17 March 1974 against Zalaegerszeg. He came on as a substitute in the second half and contributed to the 3–0 victory with a goal, the last one in his career. Albert, after receiving greetings and gifts from the old boys, the opponents and his son, ran to the stands, bowed for the fans and left the field on the shoulders of his teammates.<ref name=hetek /><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.samsungsport.hu/magyar-labdarugas/20111106/albert-sirva-bucsuzott-majd-meghajolt-a-kozonseg-elott/|title=Albert sírva búcsúzott, majd meghajolt a közönség előtt|publisher=Samsungsport.hu|date=6 November 2011|access-date=7 November 2011|language=hu|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120909192055/http://www.samsungsport.hu/magyar-labdarugas/20111106/albert-sirva-bucsuzott-majd-meghajolt-a-kozonseg-elott/|archive-date=9 September 2012}}</ref>

Following his retirement, he had two short spells as a manager in Libya with [[Al-Ahly Benghazi S.C.|Al-Ahly Benghazi]], however, with only limited success. After returning from North Africa, Albert worked for Ferencváros in several positions, such as technical director, department leader and later honorary chairman. In 2007, Ferencváros' stadium was named after him.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://budapesttimes.hu/2007/12/21/ferencvaros-stadium-renamed-after-florian-albert/|title=Ferencvaros stadium renamed after Florian Albert|work=Budapest Times|date=21 December 2007|access-date=3 November 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140712134705/http://budapesttimes.hu/2007/12/21/ferencvaros-stadium-renamed-after-florian-albert/|archive-date=12 July 2014}}</ref> In the same year, he received a prize in his village of birth, Hercegszántó, becoming an honorable citizen.<ref name="Hrvatski glasnik" /> In 2010 [[Budapest]], a year later, [[Ferencváros]] awarded him honorary citizenship.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.origo.hu/sport/magyarfoci/20111008-a-ferencvaros-diszpolgara-cimet-vehette-at-a-70-eves-albert.html|title=Ferencváros díszpolgára lett Albert Flórián|work=Hungarian Press Agency|publisher=Origo|date=8 October 2011|access-date=8 November 2011|language=hu|archive-date=14 November 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111114150410/http://www.origo.hu/sport/magyarfoci/20111008-a-ferencvaros-diszpolgara-cimet-vehette-at-a-70-eves-albert.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Albert married Irén Bársony, an actress, on 30 November 1963. The couple had two children, a girl, Magdolna, and a son, [[Flórián Albert Jr.]], who, like his father, became a football player with Ferencváros, and later had spells in Israel and France and also played for the Hungarian national team. Albert's grandchild, Flórián Patrik, aims to become a professional footballer as well.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fourfourtwo.hu/hirek/magyarorszag/a-harom-albert-florian-egyutt-volt-a-puskas-akademia-vendege|title=A három Albert Flórián együtt volt a Puskás Akadémia vendége|trans-title=The three Flórián Albert together were guests of the Puskas Academy|work=pfla.hu|publisher=[[FourFourTwo]]|date=29 August 2010|access-date=31 October 2011|language=hu|archive-date=19 January 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120119000607/http://www.fourfourtwo.hu/hirek/magyarorszag/a-harom-albert-florian-egyutt-volt-a-puskas-akademia-vendege|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Death==
[[File:Albert Flórián 2011.jpg|thumb|left|Farewell from Flórián Albert in front of the stadium named after him]]

On 27 October 2011, Flórián, after suffering a vasoconstriction, underwent coronary artery bypass surgery. Although a press release the following day by his former club Ferencváros stated that the operation had been successful,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://hvg.hu/itthon/20111031_meghalt_albert_florian|title=Meghalt Albert Flórián|trans-title=Flórián Albert died|publisher=[[Heti Világgazdaság]]|date=31 October 2011|access-date=31 October 2011|language=hu|archive-date=2 November 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111102165626/http://hvg.hu/itthon/20111031_meghalt_albert_florian|url-status=live}}</ref> he subsequently suffered a heart attack and died in the early hours of 31 October 2011.<ref name=obituary />

His funeral took place on 6 November 2011 in the Cemetery of Óbuda. Hundreds of mourners accompanied Albert to his final rest, including [[Viktor Orbán]], Prime Minister of Hungary; [[Pál Schmitt]], President of Hungary; Sándor Csányi, president of the Hungarian Football Federation; Gábor Kubatov, president of Ferencvárosi TC; and former teammates [[Kálmán Mészöly]], [[Gyula Rákosi]], [[Lajos Szűcs (footballer born 1943)|Lajos Szűcs]] and [[Tibor Nyilasi]]. The event was also live broadcast by Hungarian public television [[Magyar Televízió]].<ref name=funeral>{{cite web|url=http://uk.eurosport.yahoo.com/06112011/2/ferencvaros-held-0-0-albert-funeral.html|title=Ferencvaros held 0–0 after Albert funeral|publisher=Yahoo! Eurosport|date=6 November 2011|access-date=8 November 2011|archive-date=6 October 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221006113539/https://consent.yahoo.com/v2/collectConsent?sessionId=2_cc-session_13c40740-20fa-413a-b76f-61e847b2b4a5|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nemzetisport.hu/magyar_valogatott/orok-nyugalomra-helyeztek-albert-floriant-2101953?nocache|title=Örök nyugalomra helyezték Albert Flóriánt|publisher=Nemzeti Sport Online|date=6 November 2011|access-date=8 November 2011|language=hu|archive-date=8 November 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111108234154/http://www.nemzetisport.hu/magyar_valogatott/orok-nyugalomra-helyeztek-albert-floriant-2101953?nocache|url-status=live}}</ref>

In the afternoon same day, Ferencváros played a league clash against [[Paksi SE]]. Before the match the floodlights were switched off and the stadium turned into dark, with candles lit by the fans are being the only lights in the arena. Ferencváros players wore a special all-black kit in the occasion and fans paid tribute to Albert with a banner saying "God shall be with you Emperor".<ref name=funeral /><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nemzetisport.hu/labdarugo_nb_i/az-ftc-gol-nelkuli-dontetlennel-bucsuzott-a-csaszartol-2101985?nocache|title=Az FTC gól nélküli döntetlennel búcsúzott a Császártól|publisher=Nemzeti Sport Online|date=6 November 2011|access-date=8 November 2011|language=hu|archive-date=8 November 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111108213441/http://www.nemzetisport.hu/labdarugo_nb_i/az-ftc-gol-nelkuli-dontetlennel-bucsuzott-a-csaszartol-2101985?nocache|url-status=live}}</ref> Supporters of [[SK Rapid Wien]], who have close ties with Ferencváros, also shown honor to Albert with a transparent in their game against SV Ried.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nemzetisport.hu/nso_hirek/ausztria-a-becsi-zold-feherek-is-elkoszontek-albert-floriantol-foto-2101966?nocache|title=Ausztria: a bécsi zöld-fehérek is elköszöntek Albert Flóriántól|publisher=Nemzeti Sport Online|date=6 November 2011|access-date=8 November 2011|language=hu|archive-date=7 November 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111107165848/http://www.nemzetisport.hu/nso_hirek/ausztria-a-becsi-zold-feherek-is-elkoszontek-albert-floriantol-foto-2101966?nocache|url-status=live}}</ref>

The friendly match against [[Liechtenstein national football team|Liechtenstein]] played on 11 November was declared a memorial game for Albert by the Hungarian Football Federation. The clash was originally scheduled to take place at the [[Sóstói Stadion]], but later was moved to the [[Ferenc Puskás Stadium (1953)|Ferenc Puskás Stadium]] to give more people the opportunity to attend the event. In the four corners of the arena memorial places were erected, where the supporters could pay their tribute to the Golden Ball winner. A five-minute-long compilation of the best moments of Albert was also projected before the kick-off.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nemzetisport.hu/fogadozona/telt-hazas-tisztelges-albert-florian-emleke-elott-2102557|title=Telt házas tisztelgés Albert Flórián emléke előtt|publisher=Nemzeti Sport|date=10 November 2011|access-date=27 November 2011|language=hu|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111115141331/http://www.nemzetisport.hu/fogadozona/telt-hazas-tisztelges-albert-florian-emleke-elott-2102557|archive-date=15 November 2011}}</ref>

Hungary eventually won the match 5–0 in front of a sold-out crowd with two goals by [[Balázs Dzsudzsák]], and further strikes from [[Tamás Priskin]], [[Vladimir Koman]] and [[Róbert Feczesin]]. Dzsudzsák commented after the match that he is sure that Flórián would have been happy if he could have seen the match, and added that he hopes they rejoiced him in Heaven.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nemzetisport.hu/magyar_valogatott/gyoztes-tisztelges-albert-florian-emleke-elott-2102869|title=Győztes tisztelgés Albert Flórián emléke előtt|publisher=Nemzeti Sport|date=11 November 2011|access-date=27 November 2011|language=hu|archive-date=13 November 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111113162135/http://www.nemzetisport.hu/magyar_valogatott/gyoztes-tisztelges-albert-florian-emleke-elott-2102869|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Honours ==
'''Ferencváros'''
* [[Inter-Cities Fairs Cup]]: [[1964–65 Inter-Cities Fairs Cup|1964–65]]
* [[Nemzeti Bajnokság I|Hungarian League]]: 1963, 1964, 1967 and 1968
* [[Magyar Kupa|Hungarian Cup]]: 1972

'''Individual'''
* [[Ballon d'Or]]: [[1967 Ballon d'Or|1967]]
* [[FIFA World Cup awards#FIFA Young Player Award|World Cup Best Young Player Award]]: [[1962 FIFA World Cup|1962]]
* [[FIFA World Cup awards#Golden Boot|World Cup top scorer]]: 1962 (shared with five other players at 4 goals)
* [[FIFA World Cup awards#All-Star Team|World Cup All-Star Team]]: [[1966 FIFA World Cup|1966]]
*[[UEFA European Championship Teams of the Tournament|UEFA European Championship Team of the Tournament]]: [[1964 European Nations' Cup|1964]]<ref>{{cite news|title=1964 team of the tournament|publisher=Union of European Football Associations|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro-2020/news/0253-0d7d0bdc396b-570ad6e6ff87-1000--euro-1964-team-of-the-tournament/?iv=true|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200724153004/https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro-2020/news/0253-0d7d0bdc396b-570ad6e6ff87-1000--euro-1964-team-of-the-tournament/?iv=true|url-status=dead|archive-date=24 July 2020|access-date=14 May 2020}}</ref>
*''FUWO European Team of the Season'': 1966,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcc-supporters.org/fuwo/files/FUWO%201967/FUWO%201967%2002.pdf |website=FCC-Wiki|title=FUWO 1967|access-date=23 April 2024 }}</ref> 1967,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcc-supporters.org/fuwo/files/FUWO%201968/FUWO%201968%20%2002.pdf |website=FCC-Wiki|title=FUWO 1968|access-date=23 April 2024 }}</ref> 1968<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcc-supporters.org/fuwo/files/FUWO%201969/FUWO%201969%2002.pdf |website=FCC-Wiki|title=FUWO 1969|access-date=23 April 2024 }}</ref>
*[[Allgemeiner Deutscher Nachrichtendienst|ADN Eastern European Footballer of the Season]]: 1967<ref>{{cite web|url=http://ukrfootball.ua/news/albert-dzhayich-blohin-stoyichkov-levandovski-shcho-spilnogo |website=ukrfootball.ua |title=Eastern European Footballer of the season|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304200112/http://ukrfootball.ua/news/albert-dzhayich-blohin-stoyichkov-levandovski-shcho-spilnogo |access-date=5 July 2024 |archive-date=4 March 2016 }}</ref>
* [[List of European Cup and UEFA Champions League top scorers|European Cup top scorer]]: [[1965–66 European Cup|1965–66]]
* Inter-Cities Fairs Cup top scorer: [[1966–67 Inter-Cities Fairs Cup|1966–67]]
* Hungarian Championship top scorer: 1960, 1961, 1965
* Hungarian Footballer of the Year: 1966, 1967
* Officier's Cross of [[Order of Merit of the Republic of Hungary]]: 1994
* Middle Cross of the Order Merit of the Republic of Hungary: 2011
* Sportsperson of the Nation (A Nemzet Sportolója): 2004
* Honorable Citizen of Hercegszántó: 2007
* Honorable Citizen of Budapest: 2010
* Honorable Citizen of Ferencváros: 2011
